definition: Applying everyday knowledge about the world — physics, social norms, causality — that humans take for granted; a persistent challenge for AI systems evaluated by benchmarks like CommonsenseQA.
details: Applying everyday knowledge about the world — physics, social norms, causality — that humans take for granted; a persistent challenge for AI systems evaluated by benchmarks like CommonsenseQA.

explainer.lead: Common sense reasoning is the ability to fill in obvious gaps using everyday knowledge of objects, people, and cause and effect. It matters because an AI system can produce fluent answers while still missing conclusions that people consider immediate.

tiers.eli5: Imagine seeing a glass fall off a table: you expect it to hit the floor and perhaps spill water, without anyone explaining why. Common sense reasoning is using that kind of everyday knowledge to work out what is likely to happen. Computers can find this hard because people usually leave these obvious details unsaid.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers test whether a system can supply unstated physical, social, or causal knowledge when answering questions or choosing actions. Benchmarks such as CommonsenseQA provide evaluation settings, but passing individual questions does not establish reliable reasoning in new situations. A key pitfall is confusing a plausible answer with one justified by the situation.
tiers.paperLevel: Given an observation or question q and largely implicit everyday knowledge K, the task is to infer a conclusion c using physical, social, or causal regularities. The central difficulty is the breadth and implicit nature of K. Benchmark results, including those on CommonsenseQA, measure performance on their tasks rather than common sense reasoning in general.

explainer.example: If someone knocks a full glass off a table, a system using common sense reasoning would expect the glass to fall and the water to spill. It connects the action to its likely physical consequences even when the description does not state them.

explainer.intuition: Human communication leaves out enormous amounts of shared background knowledge. Common sense reasoning reconstructs enough of that knowledge to draw an ordinary, sensible conclusion.
howItWorks: Apply everyday physical, social, or causal knowledge.
Check which conclusion fits those expectations.
explainer.whyItMatters: Without this ability, an AI system can miss obvious consequences and give answers that sound reasonable but clash with everyday experience. CommonsenseQA is one benchmark used to evaluate parts of this challenge.
misconceptions: It is not simply memorizing facts; the knowledge must be applied to a situation.
Fluency does not demonstrate common sense reasoning.
One benchmark score does not cover all everyday reasoning.
